subject: Can't get the sesame street code to work

messages.author: 28b7830a49c6e276
messages.subject: Can't get the sesame street code to work
parts:
I'm using the following from the Stan example code. There seems to be a problem with the data model. I keep getting the following error and the model does not get past the warmup stage:
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Invalid value of Sigma_yt: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: Sigma_ytSigma_yt is not positive definite. Sigma_yt(0,0) is 2.4018295391036435e-13:0.

If anyone has any advice, please let me know.

data {
  int<lower=0> J;
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=1,upper=J> siteset[N];
  matrix[N,2] yt;
  vector[N] z;
}
parameters {
  matrix[J,2] ag;
  real b;
  real d;
  real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_ag;
  real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_yt;
  vector[2] mu_ag;
  real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_a;
  real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_g;
  real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_t;
  real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] a;
  vector[J] g;
  cov_matrix[2] Sigma_ag;
  cov_matrix[2] Sigma_yt;
  matrix[N,2] yt_hat;

  //data level
  Sigma_yt[1,1] <- pow(sigma_y,2);
  Sigma_yt[2,2] <- pow(sigma_t,2);
  Sigma_yt[1,2] <- rho_yt*sigma_y*sigma_t;  
  Sigma_yt[2,1] <- Sigma_yt[1,2];
   
  // group level
  Sigma_ag[1,1] <- pow(sigma_a,2);
  Sigma_ag[2,2] <- pow(sigma_g,2);
  Sigma_ag[1,2] <- rho_ag*sigma_a*sigma_g;
  Sigma_ag[2,1] <- Sigma_ag[1,2];  

  for (j in 1:J) {
    a[j] <- ag[j,1];
    g[j] <- ag[j,2];
  }

  for (i in 1:N) {
    yt_hat[i,2] <- g[siteset[i]] + d * z[i];
    yt_hat[i,1] <- a[siteset[i]] + b * yt[i,2];
  }
}
model {
  //data level
  sigma_y ~ uniform (0, 100);               
  sigma_t ~ uniform (0, 100);                  
  rho_yt ~ uniform(-1, 1);
  d ~ normal (0, .001);
  b ~ normal (0, .001);

  //group level
  sigma_a ~ uniform (0, 100);
  sigma_g ~ uniform (0, 100);
  rho_ag ~ uniform(-1, 1);
  mu_ag[1] ~ normal (0, .001);
  mu_ag[2] ~ normal (0, .001);

  //data model
  for (i in 1:N)
    transpose(yt[i]) ~ multi_normal(transpose(yt_hat[i]),Sigma_yt);

  for (j in 1:J)
    transpose(ag[j]) ~ multi_normal(mu_ag,Sigma_ag);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can't get the sesame street code to work
parts:
On 1/14/14, 2:27 PM, Christopher Grainger wrote:
> I'm using the following from the Stan example code. There seems to be a
> problem with the data model. I keep getting the
> following error and the model does not get past the warmup stage:
> Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of
> the following issue: Invalid
> value of Sigma_yt: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: Sigma_ytSigma_yt is not positive
> definite. Sigma_yt(0,0) is 2.4018295391036435e-13:0.
>
> If anyone has any advice, please let me know.

Thanks for the error report. Two parts to the response.

1. The underlying problem is that we mistranslated the
original BUGS model, which has lines like

d ~ normal(0, .001);

BUGS uses a precision-based parameterization of normal, whereas
Stan uses a standard-deviation-based parameterization. So these
should be normal(0,31.6) to match the BUGS code.

There are other issues with that translation, too. It's
not using vectorization (not that it'll matter much here)
and I believe all of the transformed parameters should just
be local variables in the model (otherwise you're going to
get a bunch of junk in the output). I made both of those changes, too.

I only fixed sesame_street1.stan, which now runs with reasonable
mixing. It takes a while to warmup, but then samples very quickly
once it's adapted.

I've bcc-ed the original author of these and am going to
ask that they be reviewed for this kind of error and that they're
checked that they get the right answer.

Sorry about this --- we should be more careful in this kind
of thing as users will assume we've done them right since they're
our models to begin with!


2. The messages you're getting are just warnings. They weren't
the source of the problem.

What's happening is that the gradient-based approximation
of the posterior is only approximate and following the gradient
can take you outside of support on highly-constrained parameters
like covariance matrices.

You'll still see a few of them with the fixed model.

- Bob

P.S. Here's the text of the revised model:

data {
int<lower=0> J;
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=1,upper=J> siteset[N];

vector[2] yt[N];
vector[N] z;
}
parameters {
vector[2] ag[J];

real b;
real d;
real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_ag;
real<lower=-1,upper=1> rho_yt;
vector[2] mu_ag;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_a;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_g;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_t;
real<lower=0,upper=100> sigma_y;
}
model {

vector[J] a;
vector[J] g;

matrix[2,2] Sigma_ag;
matrix[2,2] Sigma_yt;
vector[2] yt_hat[N];

//data level
Sigma_yt[1,1] <- pow(sigma_y,2);
Sigma_yt[2,2] <- pow(sigma_t,2);
Sigma_yt[1,2] <- rho_yt*sigma_y*sigma_t;
Sigma_yt[2,1] <- Sigma_yt[1,2];

// group level
Sigma_ag[1,1] <- pow(sigma_a,2);
Sigma_ag[2,2] <- pow(sigma_g,2);
Sigma_ag[1,2] <- rho_ag*sigma_a*sigma_g;
Sigma_ag[2,1] <- Sigma_ag[1,2];

for (j in 1:J) {
a[j] <- ag[j,1];
g[j] <- ag[j,2];
}

for (i in 1:N) {
yt_hat[i,2] <- g[siteset[i]] + d * z[i];
yt_hat[i,1] <- a[siteset[i]] + b * yt[i,2];
}

//data level
sigma_y ~ uniform (0, 100);
sigma_t ~ uniform (0, 100);
rho_yt ~ uniform(-1, 1);

d ~ normal (0, 31.6);
b ~ normal (0, 31.6);

//group level
sigma_a ~ uniform (0, 100);
sigma_g ~ uniform (0, 100);
rho_ag ~ uniform(-1, 1);
mu_ag ~ normal (0, 31.6);
for (j in 1:J)
ag[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_ag,Sigma_ag);

//data model
for (i in 1:N)
yt[i] ~ multi_normal(yt_hat[i],Sigma_yt);

}
